children: The US dollar fell after Democrats swept Congress in the US Midterms, as lower yields and policy uncertainty weighed. The DXY hit 101.10 on November 4, a five-week low and 1.7% below October’s 18-month peak of 102.87, according to BeInCrypto. It was up about 4% in 2026 and rebounded to 102.28 on November 6. The 10-year yield slid to 4.92% from around 5.3% in early October; October job growth of 165,000 beat expectations, lifting bets on a December Fed rate hike. Dollar weakness may favor stocks and crypto, though Bitcoin fell more than 5% in the AI-led selloff. Inflation, Fed signals and DXY support at 100.90–101.15 are key; a break below 100.90 could expose 100.20–100.60 and 99.

title: Why Is the US Dollar Falling? Midterms, Yields and a Critical Economic Test
